finding.claim: The avatar endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The only check is that the URL starts with "https://", which does not restrict the host. An attacker can target internal or cloud-metadata hosts that serve HTTPS, such as https://users.internal, https://localhost, or internal services with TLS. Axios follows redirects by default (up to 5), so an attacker-controlled HTTPS server can also redirect to http:// internal targets such as http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/. The response is not returned, but the byte length is. That gives a blind and size-oracle SSRF, and it can also be used for port scanning or timing probes.

trace.note: Only checks typeof string and startsWith("https://")
axios.get(url) issues the request, following redirects by default
Response size is returned to the caller (img.data.length)

finding.guards_checked: The scheme prefix check (https://) is the only guard. There is no host or IP allowlist, no DNS resolution or private-range blocking, no maxRedirects:0 or redirect validation, and no authentication on the route. The https check does not stop internal hosts or redirects to http.

verdict.guard_found: none (only typeof string and startsWith("https://") prefix check at server.js:11)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route (server.js:9, no auth middleware, only express.json at :5), server.js:11 applies only a scheme prefix check, and server.js:14 calls axios.get with default redirect following and returns the byte length at :15.
